A thesis questionnaire measuring how well organised attendees found an event, on a 4-item Likert scale with 1 reverse-worded item. surveyframe declares the analysis in advance (Scale score descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha (internal consistency), McDonald's omega (internal consistency), Item diagnostics) and reports it in APA 7.

## In SurveyStudio

In RStudio, open the Addins menu, choose **surveyframe: Try a demo** and pick `likert_scale`. The study opens on the Design screen. Plan shows each research question with its method and decision rule, Analyse runs them as declared, and Report writes the APA 7 report.

![The Design screen with the likert_scale study.](../../templates/likert_scale/design.png){width=100%}

## In R

```r
d <- sframe_demo("likert_scale")
results <- run_analysis_plan(d$responses, d$instrument)
render_report(d$instrument, d$responses)
```

## What the report gives

| Research question | Method | What the report gives |
|---|---|---|
| How does the scale score overall? | Descriptive statistics | The APA 7 sentence, its table and chart |
| Is the scale internally consistent? | Cronbach's alpha (internal consistency) | The APA 7 sentence, its table and chart |
| Same question, omega rather than alpha. | McDonald's omega (internal consistency) | The APA 7 sentence, its table and chart |
| Does any item sit poorly with the rest? | Item diagnostics | The APA 7 sentence, its table and chart |

The demo's data is simulated, so the site shows no numbers. Run it in SurveyStudio or R to see the results, each marked as demonstration data.
